run.question: My application to switch from a Graduate visa to a Skilled Worker visa, made inside the UK, was refused on 28 September 2026 because the Home Office does not think the job is genuine. Which gives me the best chance: an administrative review, a fresh application or getting a solicitor to challenge it in court?

answer.summary: I can't say which route gives you the best chance, because that is legal advice about your case. Note that if you applied in the UK, an administrative review must be requested within 14 calendar days of receiving the refusal notice, and asking for a review then making a new application withdraws the review.

claims.text: For an application made in the UK, the time limit for an administrative review is 14 calendar days from the date you receive the refusal notice, or 7 if you are detained.

citations.quote: It is 14 calendar days from the date the applicant receives the refusal notice (seven calendar days if they are detained).

claims.text: An administrative review costs £80 and you apply online.

citations.quote: You can apply online for an administrative review. It costs £80.

claims.text: An administrative review lets you raise a permitted casework error, and a different person on an independent team carries it out.

citations.quote: It will allow the applicant to raise any permitted case work error (defined in Appendix Administrative Review) that they think has been made on the application and, if an error has been made, have it corrected.

claims.text: If you ask for an administrative review and then make a new application, the review is treated as withdrawn.

citations.quote: If an applicant makes an administrative review application and then makes a new application for entry clearance, permission to enter or permission to stay, the administrative review application will be treated as withdrawn.

claims.text: If the administrative review is unsuccessful and you have no immigration permission, you must leave the UK.

citations.quote: The applicant must leave the UK after they receive the administrative review decision if they do not have immigration permission.

answer.declined_reason: Choosing between an administrative review, a fresh application and a court challenge depends on the facts of your case, so it is a personal judgement and legal advice. Please speak urgently to a registered immigration adviser or a solicitor, and see the GOV.UK page 'Ask for a visa administrative review' (https://www.gov.uk/ask-for-a-visa-administrative-review/if-youre-in-the-uk). Your deadline may be very close.

run.question: I'm on a Student visa for a four-year integrated master's, but I'm going to finish early, after three years, with the bachelor's degree, and my company will then sponsor me for a Skilled Worker visa. What happens to my Student visa, will my university handle the change from four years to three or is that something I have to do myself, and is there anything I need to do before I can switch?

answer.summary: Your university must tell the Home Office within 10 working days if it stops sponsoring you because you finish sooner than expected or move to another sponsored visa. Before you switch, you must have completed the course you were sponsored for, and leaving an integrated master's with the lower degree counts as completing it. I couldn't confirm from the guidance what happens to your Student visa's end date after the university reports this, or whether you need to tell the Home Office anything yourself. For that, ask your university's visa team or a registered immigration adviser.

claims.text: Leaving an integrated master's programme with the lower qualification counts as successfully completing the course your CAS was for.
